A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MoDec-GS framework. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction experiments on iPhone, HyperNeRF and Nvidia datasets, component ablations and motion analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds MoDec-GS results on D-NeRF and PanopticSports, timing and hyperparameter studies, and masked optical-flow analysis.

M1.justification: GLMD, GAD, LGD, anchor dynamics and TIA retain the same procedures, method equations and Algorithm 1. Appendix C expands the description of existing Scaffold-GS and HexPlane components without establishing an algorithm or architecture change.

E1.justification: v2 adds evaluations on synthetic D-NeRF scenes and real-world PanopticSports scenes in Appendix F.3, Tables 5–6. These broaden scene and motion coverage beyond the three retained real-world monocular benchmarks.

E2.justification: The new comparisons introduce C.D.3DGS on D-NeRF and Dynamic 3DGS, STG and TC-3DGS on PanopticSports as evaluated comparators. Their scores are explicitly sourced from prior work. Comparator membership in the retained experiments is unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds controlled timing of one-stage versus two-stage deformation, hyperparameter sweeps and object-masked flow evaluation. Existing benchmark splits, budgets and metrics remain stated as before. Table 8 labels N_offset=10 as the main-experiment default, conflicting with 20 in both versions’ implementation sections; an actual default change is unresolved.

E4.justification: Appendix G adds rendering-overhead measurements, sensitivity studies for HexPlane resolution, voxel size and Gaussian count, and quantified masked-flow analysis of global versus local motion. The original component ablations, TIA analysis and GLMD visualization are retained; the latter moves from Appendix E.1 to G.3.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. Averaging over frames and sequences remains unchanged; the gradient statistics inside TIA are algorithmic quantities.

E6.justification: Original Tables 1–4 and the detailed results in v1 Table 5, now v2 Table 9, retain their numerical values. New results include MoDec-GS at 33.25 dB and 8 MB on D-NeRF, 27.96 dB and 34 MB on PanopticSports, plus timing, sensitivity and masked-flow outcomes. These are added evaluations, not same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: Appendix C adds explicit mathematical descriptions of scaled anchor offsets and multiscale HexPlane feature construction, particularly Eqs. 15 and 17. This is a limited formal elaboration of existing components; the original equations and TIA algorithm remain unchanged, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: compact dynamic reconstruction through GLMD and adaptive TIA. The claims of approximately 70% average storage reduction and improved or maintained rendering quality are unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix G.4 explicitly interprets global motion as rigid interval transformations and local motion as non-rigid deformation between time steps. v2 also discusses the new overhead and quality–storage trade-offs. The Nvidia tOF exclusion is re-explained through sparse temporal test views; the thin-texture failure limitation remains unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 itemizes storage accounting as the global scaffold, deformation fields, attribute MLPs and canonical-time list. It adds an explicit HexPlane construction description, a direct demo-video link and a planned code-release route. The existing implementation settings and hardware disclosures are largely retained.

R1.justification: The concurrent-work discussion moves to Appendix D and adds Relay-GS. The earlier specific criticism of 4D Scaffold-GS’s piecewise-linear motion assumption disappears, while the monocular-data distinction remains. References supporting the added datasets, TC-3DGS comparison and SAM 2 masking expand the bibliography without redefining the main research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 polishes wording throughout the retained text, expands preliminary explanations, moves demo information before implementation details, relocates concurrent-work discussion and adds acknowledgements. The main narrative and method-section organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds four tables for benchmarks, timing and sensitivity, plus an anchor-representation schematic and masked-flow figure. These substantially expand the visual evidence. Existing benchmark tables, qualitative comparisons, GLMD visualization and failure examples are retained with relocation, renumbering and limited caption or label edits.

improvement.justification: The additional benchmarks and targeted overhead, sensitivity and motion studies strengthen the evidence for generalization and practical trade-offs, while clearer storage accounting improves transparency. The gain is limited by brief protocol documentation for the added benchmarks and the new N_offset inconsistency between Table 8 and Appendix B. The core method and previously reported results remain stable.
